issue.body:
Implements contracts (https://github.com/NixOS/rfcs/pull/189) by building on the work by @ibizaman (and [earlier work](https://github.com/fricklerhandwerk/module-interfaces) by @fricklerhandwerk).

Closes https://github.com/NixOS/rfcs/pull/189.

For more info, see the [manual entry](https://github.com/KiaraGrouwstra/nixpkgs/blob/contracts-automated/nixos/doc/manual/development/contracts.md) or [options reference](https://kiaragrouwstra.github.io/contracts/options.html#opt-contractTypes).

Supersedes: #432529, #485453, #495303, #500287.

Disclaimer: I have made use of a coding agent to get things to this state.

## Use-cases

- [abstracting over alternate providers](https://shb.skarabox.com/contracts.html#contracts-why)
- modular services: porting legacy modules consisting of multiple services (#490688)

## Differences from the RFC

1. **Topology: point-to-point vs aggregated:** The RFC has each consumer directly link to one provider (consumer.provider = config.services.restic...), with bidirectional references (provider.consumer = config.services.nextcloud...). We use centralized aggregation - consumers register into `contracts.<type>.want`, providers register into `contracts.<type>.providers`, and a `defaultProvider`/`defaultProviderName` selects which provider fulfills all requests. This avoids the 'dual-link' problem the RFC mentioned.
1. **[Modular service](https://nixos.org/manual/nixos/stable/#modular-services) support:** The RFC doesn't address modular services. We implement  a bridge pattern to give modular services the same API for using contracts as NixOS modules.
1. **Cross-system support:** The RFC is NixOS-only. Our `lib/contracts/module.nix` and `lib/services/` are system-agnostic, designed to pave the way for contracts support from other systems managing nix (modular) services, e.g. home-manager, nimi, nix-darwin, finix, NixBSD, etc.
1. **Contract type registration:** The RFC defines contracts inline as `contracts.<name>` with `deferredModule` types. We separate type definitions (`contractTypes`) from instances (`contracts`), with types shipped in `lib.contracts` (usable from the sandbox for docs builds) and extensible from outside nixpkgs via `config.contractTypes` (without such docs).
1. **Naming: input/output vs request/result:** The RFC uses input/output. We use request/result. This is more specific about the directionality (a consumer requests, a provider produces results), and more consistent with [SelfHostBlocks](https://github.com/ibizaman/selfhostblocks).

## Tests to run on changes

- `bash lib/tests/modules.sh`
- `nix-instantiate --eval lib/services/test.nix`
- `nix-build -A nixosTests.contracts`
- `nix-build -A stash.passthru.tests.stash`
- `nix-build nixos/release.nix -A manual.x86_64-linux`

## Next steps

None of these are breaking changes necessarily, so may not need to be in-scope for the initial PR:

- [ ] [optional feature support within a contract](https://github.com/KiaraGrouwstra/nixpkgs/compare/contracts-automated...KiaraGrouwstra:nixpkgs:contracts-tags) as suggested [on discourse](https://discourse.nixos.org/t/pre-rfc-decouple-services-using-structured-typing/58257/43) (still wanna think this over, not sure how i feel about it yet)
- [ ] add support for more systems ([home-manager](https://github.com/nix-community/home-manager/compare/master...KiaraGrouwstra:home-manager:contracts), ...)
- [ ] add more contracts (e.g. [draft](https://github.com/KiaraGrouwstra/nixpkgs/compare/contracts-automated...contracts-new-types))
- [ ] validate the implementation thru further real-life experience

review_comments.body:
I find this more readable, espacially when seeing the wiring in the other direction, right after.

```
contracts.databaseConnection.want.webapp.db = config.services.webapp.db;
```
What does this do? up there I have to wire providers and consumers. what does a default do here?

Maybe the diagram shadows a bit, the information in the next paragraph are very informative, but kinda miss in the diagram. I understand your test setup like this.

```
webapp <-[databaseConnection]-- pgProvider <--[fileSecret]-- hardcoded-secret
```
review_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,141 @@
+# Tests contract chaining: a provider that is also a consumer.
+#
+# Chain: webapp <- databaseConnection <- fileSecrets

review_comments.body:
is the `databaseConnection` contract tied to webapp? meaning would `webapp` use the same contract?

Could I for example add this service wiring, next to the wiring up there, on the same machine?

```
anotherWebapp <-[databaseConnection]-- pgProvider <--[fileSecret]-- another-hardcoded-secret
yetanotherWebapp <-[databaseConnection]-- localhostpgProvider
```
review_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,141 @@
+# Tests contract chaining: a provider that is also a consumer.
+#
+# Chain: webapp <- databaseConnection <- fileSecrets
+#
+# - `webapp` (consumer): requests a database connection via the
+#   `databaseConnection` contract and reads `result.connectionString`.

review_comments.body:
I don't understand what happens here. 
Is there any situation where, this option (which is of contract type databaseConnection) has another value as the one you set here?
Maybe the parameter should be default to this, and be `readonly = true` (https://noogle.dev/f/lib/mkOption/)

review_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,141 @@
+# Tests contract chaining: a provider that is also a consumer.
+#
+# Chain: webapp <- databaseConnection <- fileSecrets
+#
+# - `webapp` (consumer): requests a database connection via the
+#   `databaseConnection` contract and reads `result.connectionString`.

review_comments.body:
contract requests may be fulfilled by any provider matching the contract.
the defaults make for an easy way to say you want any requests for a given contract handled by a given type of provider, so as to prevent having to wire each one manually - tho such overrides are still possible, in case you don't want them all handled the same way.

they're boilerplate.
i managed to move the first line to `default` now, as you suggested.
`readOnly = true` i unfortunately didn't get to work yet, somehow triggering 'option set twice' type of errors.
